**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

## What looks good

- `simulate` takes the history out and grows it with `Arc::make_mut` (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/cut.rs:161-163`). With one owner, no copy occurs. A second stock that holds the `Arc` keeps the old history. The copy happens one time, and only when the stock shares the history.
- The copy is a `History` clone. The `cuts` `Vec` keeps its order, and `add_ops` only appends (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/carry_history.rs:97`). A growth cannot lose or add a cut twice.
- A refusal before the history is taken (`check_ops`, posed moves) leaves the stock as it was. A refusal after it restores the old cut count with `h.cuts.truncate(n)` (`cut.rs:164`, `cut.rs:173-174`). `add_ops` writes only `cuts`, so the restore is exact.
- The stock's history is `None` during the cut. No cut path reads it. The only references are `Dexel::block` (`dexel.rs:63`) and the carry and tile constructors. The temporary `None` changes no reading.
- The active side-on path reads the grown history with `h.read(false)` (`cut.rs:165`). `read` stores `Arc::new(self.clone())` in the returned `Dexel` (`carry_exact.rs:157`). The new cuts stay. That path runs one time for each setup, as the body says.
- The growth is amortised. The one-owner call appends in O(1), and `Vec` grows with a doubling policy. The history size is bounded by the number of non-rapid moves. The active read has a named budget refusal (`carry_exact.rs:124`). The change adds no index or cast.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic` outside tests. No new dependency. The net diff is three `crates/sim` files. No golden or snapshot change.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- The issue asks for a time budget in its "Done means". The new tests pin the in-place growth with `Arc` pointer identity and the per-call stock against the one-call stock bit for bit. They do not assert a time. I read the old code: the pointer pin fails there, because each call made a new `Arc`. The body gives the readings.
- A caller that keeps a `Dexel` clone across calls still copies the history on each call. That is correct copy-on-write. The fix covers the one-owner case that the report describes.
- The first commit is the fork's process sync (`PROCESS_VERSION` 145 to 149). The merge with main drops it. The net diff has no process file, so no `Process change:` line is needed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
